video.title: Why Jacob Zuma is South Africa's Zulu Ninja Turtle | Trevor Noah

protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Lemonfox transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Hook: 'We got the cutest president in the world, and you guys don't respect him' -- the grin, 'like one of those kids in Jet magazine', 'he looks like a little Zulu Ninja Turtle... Leonardo, Raphael, Michelangelo, Jacob. Cowabunga.' Opening at 50.5 ('How could you hate on Jacob Zuma?') also works but runs 18s.

Hook: an American article says 'ANC Youth League marches over painting' -- 'a move in the right direction, the youth should focus on arts and culture' -- he pictures them marching: 'Picasso! We are sick and tired of postmodernistic impressionalism. We demand more sketch art.' Payoff at 122.6.

Hook: 'Jacob Zuma did not complain once because he understands art' -- the guys around him run to him tattletaling like kids: 'They painted you! They painted you!' -- Zuma: 'There's no paint on me. I'm fine.' Lands at 248.1; running on through 'I don't see anything wrong with this at all' and the long Zuma giggle (273.3) also works.

Hook: 'I wouldn't be shocked if Jacob's having the time of his life right now in the presidential bedroom' -- that many wives, body paint, Barry White, at the door of wife number two: 'Are you ready for the spear?' 'I'm not ready.' 'Ready or not, here I come.' The innuendo lands without knowing the painting's name. 'I hope I can hide at your houses after this' is an acceptable tag.

In a New York shop, $3,000 shoes: 'Ah, voetsek' -- 'in my culture it means thank you very much, but no' -- salesman: 'You learn something new every day. Voetsek.' -- then a woman in the corner goes 'Woo! Hello!' -- 'never seen someone so happy to hear that word.' Payoff at the woman (413.8) and his line after it (421.9).

At the taco truck window: 'You want tacos?' 'It would be awkward if I didn't' ... 'Here's your taco. You want a napkin?' -- 'on our side of the world a napkin is that thing babies wear to hold their shit.' Payoff at 527.0; 'He was trying to say serviette' is an acceptable tag.

also_ok.why: The Youth League bit run on to what the painting actually was: Zuma in black, red and yellow, 'wind blowing through where he'd have hair... just him, Jay-Z and Mini-Me. Although it wasn't that many.' Second payoff, 62s.

'People say this picture is racist, disrespectful' -- the name was strong: 'the spear, symbol of the Zulu nation... It's not like that guy called it the pocket knife.' Works, but viewers need to know what the painting shows.
The taco-truck napkin bit run on through the misunderstanding: 'Why would I want a napkin?' 'For the mess afterwards... one minute you think you got it, then it's coming out.' Bigger laugh, but 87s.

negatives.why: 'Don't you laugh at my president? Damn you, people!' -- scolding the room over its laughter at Zuma's name; room-only.
'You people were torturing him while I was away, painting horrible pictures of Jacob Zuma' -- run-up to the painting story.
'You miss so many things from South Africa... language is such a fundamental thing' -- transitional.
'They don't say orange, they say orange' -- the joke is all in the accents, and it restates 'you miss your languages'.
